summary: This is just a note to you both to wish you happiness this Christmas, which you both deserve. Don’t be depressed, Mike, like you tend to be this time of year. We have a saying down here: “Things are worse that I hoped.” Remember that, for whatever it’s worth (it’s worth nothing but it makes the time pass). Our city here is clean and modern and very urban, except that now and then a giant tumbleweed comes rolling down the street past the apartment complexes. We all go out and stare at it uncomprehendingly. It goes on by, with the same attitude toward us. I believe they—the tumbleweeds—were here first, then the orangegroves, then us. We refuse to treat them as equals, however. I’ve been writing again, after over two years of silence. Mike—here is an improvement on the statement, “Life is brutal, nasty and short.” It goes, “Life is brutal, nasty and long,” which is worse. I put that in here because I am writing stuff like that, sort of wise new sayings. Down here they (i.e. the tumbleweeds) consider me brilliant (that should tell you something about the area). For exam­ ple, there was an article in the December issue of Crawdaddy, the rock magazine, in which was said, “He is one of the great minds of our generation.” That cer­ tainly is true. In the accompanying picture I am gazing at Wanda Kendall, a friend of mine who is a belly dancer. The Great Mind is thinking true to form.
